title: Sort list
description: Given a list of Strings, use a lambda with Comparator to sort them by length (from shortest to longest). Print the sorted list.
hints: Comparator is a functional interface: you can use a lambda like (a, b) -> a.length() - b.length()
You can also use Comparator.comparingInt(String::length) with a method reference
Collections.sort(lista, comparator) modifies the list in-place
solutionExplanation: The lambda (a, b) -> a.length() - b.length() creates a Comparator that compares by length. If the result is negative, a goes before b.

title: Filter and transform
description: Given a list of integers, use a Predicate with a lambda to filter only the even numbers, and then use a Function with a lambda to double each value. Print the results of each step.
solutionExplanation: Predicate with lambda n -> n % 2 == 0 filters even numbers. Function with lambda n -> n * 2 doubles each value. They are combined with stream().filter() and stream().map().

title: Custom operation
description: Create your own functional interface called OperacionNumerica with a method int operar(int a, int b). Then create a static method aplicarOperacion that receives two integers and an OperacionNumerica, and returns the result. Use lambdas to test with addition, subtraction and multiplication.
hints: @FunctionalInterface validates that the interface has exactly one abstract method
The OperacionNumerica interface has only: int operar(int a, int b);
The lambdas are: (a, b) -> a + b, (a, b) -> a - b, (a, b) -> a * b
solutionExplanation: OperacionNumerica is a functional interface with a single method, which allows using lambdas. The aplicarOperacion method acts as a higher-order function: it receives a function as a parameter and applies it.
